overview: Black develops both knights to the rim with 1...Na6 and 2...Nh6, which White meets by simply occupying the centre with 2.e4. White then plays d4 or c4, builds a broad centre and develops freely while Black takes time to regroup. The line is mostly a surprise weapon with little forcing play.

white_ideas.idea: Build a big centre with d4 and c4
Develop Bd3 or Be2 and castle

typical_structures.structure: White centre pawns on d4/e4 against rim knights

character.notes: Slow, unforcing play where White has an easy game and Black hopes White overpresses.

soundness.notes: Black is not refuted but the knights are misplaced and White develops freely.

structure.notes: The centre is not yet defined and White takes it.

approach.notes: Played for fun or surprise, seldom by strong players.

level.notes: Little to learn but the line is not a good first choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Other 2nd moves for White
sublines_that_differ.how: a different set-up with no e4 pawn

character.reason: Neither side is under tactical pressure and White just builds a centre.

soundness.reason: The two rim knights lose time and strong players expect White to be better.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided at move three.

approach.reason: It is a joke-style response played for surprise.

level.reason: Dubious lines are not beginner choices.

plans.reason: White takes the centre while Black rearranges.
